title: Story worlds as data entries
summary: A future-growth sketch: character arcs, personalities, open-world hubs, and participatory data entries on linked Showmob pages—using today’s blocks, with honest local-only limits.

blocks.eyebrow: Growth sketch · not shipped as a story-world tool
blocks.title: A story world of data entries readers can join
blocks.body: This page is a product sketch, not a claim that Showmob ships novels or RPG hubs end-to-end today. The growth idea is a world made of authored data entries—character arcs, personalities, places, factions, threads, items, and choices—linked as ordinary Showmob pages. Readers explore non-linearly and participate lightly. Today that participation is local-only and resets; durable state waits for a thin data layer that earns its keep.

blocks.title: Growth sketch, not a finished story-world product
blocks.body: Nothing here adds widgets, schema, or persistence. What works today is ordinary Showmob: published JSON pages, series and tags for navigation, and exercise/checklist state that lives in this browser only. Refresh, another device, or a cleared site store starts clean. Branching that sticks, unlockable secrets that survive, and shared annotations are not built. Every “later” line is optional backlog, not a promise.

nodes.title: Character arcs
nodes.detail: How people change: beats, before/after, and stakes sketched with timeline, checklist, and diagram.

nodes.title: Personalities
nodes.detail: Structured character entries: traits, voice, relationships, and secrets that unlock later—compact-table and text today.

nodes.title: Open world
nodes.detail: Places, factions, and threads as linked artifacts with tags and hubs—browse non-linearly, not only chapter order.

nodes.title: Participatory data entries
nodes.detail: Authored entries readers interact with (choices, checks, reveals). Local now; thin data layer later if a draft proves it.

blocks.heading: Theme → today’s blocks → honest limit
blocks.caption: Same renderer. Story-world jobs, not new block types.
rows: Author-written beats. No live arc map tied to reader progress.
Copied fields per page. No reusable character-card widget.
Links and tags are manual. No graph UI or auto hub.
State is local-only and resets. Nothing reaches a server or the author.

blocks.heading: How people change
blocks.body: An arc is not screenwriting jargon—it is a data shape: who starts where, what pressure forces a turn, what they become, and what it costs. On Showmob you sketch that with a timeline of beats, a before/after checklist or table, and a short stakes diagram. Name the chapter or scene slug in the detail text when a beat belongs to a specific page; diagrams do not create clickable links today.

blocks.heading: Arc layers you can already sketch

nodes.title: Beats
nodes.detail: Timeline items: open fault line → rising cost → irreversible choice → consequence.

nodes.title: Before / after
nodes.detail: Checklist or compact-table: want, wound, turn, new stance. Update when the turn page ships.

nodes.title: Stakes
nodes.detail: Diagram: pressure → choice → consequence → harder pressure. Escalate on the page, not only in notes.

items.title: Establish the fault line
items.detail: Personality entry states the starting want and wound. Opening scene page carries the first irreversible fact.

items.title: Cost becomes visible
items.detail: Mid-thread pages escalate stakes. Arc timeline names what stalls if they refuse to change.

items.title: Choice that cannot be undone
items.detail: One page owns the turn. Before/after checklist updates after that publish—not when you plan to write it.

items.title: Consequence lands
items.detail: Closing pages bill the cost. Personality entry’s new stance and open secrets get a pass.

items.label: Every major turn has a home page
items.detail: If a beat only lives in your head, put it on that page’s timeline or it will drift.

items.label: Before/after updates after publish
items.detail: Want, turn, and cost change when the page ships, not when the outline hopes they will.

items.label: Stakes escalate on the page
items.detail: If pressure does not get harder, the diagram is decoration—cut or rewrite the middle.

items.label: Name the slug in plain text
items.detail: Reference chapter or location slugs in detail strings. Do not pretend diagram nodes are links.

blocks.heading: Structured character entries
blocks.body: A personality is a reusable data entry: traits, voice, relationships, and secrets the reader may unlock later. Today you author that as a published page (or a section on a hub) with compact-table rows and prose. There is no character-card widget yet—copy the shape when you need it on another page, or link to the personality slug from resource-lists.

blocks.heading: Example personality fields (today’s shape)
blocks.caption: Author data. Interaction for secrets is local check-in only until durability earns a build.
rows: Short labels: temperament, competence, blind spot.
How they speak; one sample line as a quote block.
Who they owe, fear, or protect—name the other personality slug in the cell.
Author lists secrets; a local exercise can “reveal” one in this browser only.
Pointer to the character-arc beats that change this entry.

blocks.title: Later: character card — not shipped
blocks.body: A reusable character-card block (traits, voice, relationships, secret gates) would earn a build only if copying tables across pages becomes the blocker on a real draft. Until then, keep personalities as ordinary pages.

blocks.heading: Places, factions, and threads—non-linear
blocks.body: A story world is not only a chapter spine. Places, factions, and plot threads are explorables: readers hop via hub pages, tags, and resource-list links instead of reading one forced order. Series still helps when you want a guided path; tags and hubs carry the open map. Link artifacts by URL in resource-list items; put slug names in diagram/text details when you are only documenting the graph.

nodes.title: Place / faction page
nodes.detail: One artifact: text for lore, compact-table for who holds power, resource-list out to related entries.

nodes.title: Thread page
nodes.detail: A living plot strand: timeline of reveals, checklist of open questions, links to scenes that touch it.

nodes.title: Hub
nodes.detail: A landing artifact with resource-lists and tags that fan out—enter from any doorway.

nodes.title: Tags + series
nodes.detail: Tags for non-linear browse; series.order when a guided sequence still matters.

blocks.heading: Thin first open-world sketch (today)
items: Publish a hub page with resource-list links to a few personality, place, and thread slugs.
Tag those artifacts consistently (e.g. world, faction, thread) so the catalog stays browsable.
Use series only for paths that must stay ordered; leave the rest of the map free.
On place and thread pages, name related slugs in tables and detail text; use resource-list when you need a real URL.
Do not invent a map widget until a real world draft cannot navigate with hubs and links.

blocks.heading: Entries readers interact with
blocks.body: Participation means authored data entries—characters, locations, items, choices—that a reader can poke: mark a choice, tick a reveal, pace a cold read. The entries are content. The interaction is thin. Today exercise answers and checklist ticks stay in this browser and reset. Later, a thin data layer could persist those marks without turning Showmob into a social CMS.

columns.name: Today (shipped, local-only)
columns.detail: Exercise and checklist state live in this browser. Slideshow pacing is per visit. Refresh or another device starts clean. Nothing is saved to a server or shared with the author.

columns.name: Later (not shipped)
columns.detail: Durable choices, unlockable secrets that survive, room reactions, shared annotations, and co-author draft handoff—via a thin data layer and only if a real story-world draft proves local state is not enough.

blocks.heading: Entry kinds readers might touch
blocks.caption: Author the entry as a page or block set. Interaction stays in the existing widget bin.
rows: compact-table or text on a loot/thread page
Pick an option; answer resets on refresh

blocks.heading: Example reader check-in (local only — resets)
blocks.prompt: For a participatory story world, what should Showmob support first while staying thin?
options: A full forum and live co-edit under every entry
Authored entries plus a single local choice or check that resets until durability is proven
A new persistence layer and branching engine before any world pages ship
blocks.explanation: Local exercise and checklist already cover a thin poke. Forums, live co-edit, and a persistence engine are other products. Persist a choice only when a real draft shows local reset is not enough.
blocks.correctFeedback: Right—authored entries first, local poke second, durable layer only when evidence demands it.
blocks.wrongFeedback: Heavier social, editing, or persistence surfaces are out of scope for this growth sketch. Prefer entries plus one local check first.

blocks.heading: What would earn a later build (not shipped)

items.label: Character-card block — not shipped
items.detail: Reusable traits, voice, relationships, secret gates. Today: compact-table + text + checklist per page.

items.label: Arc-map / world-graph — not shipped
items.detail: Structured map of arcs and places linked to slugs. Today: diagram + timeline + resource-list hubs.

items.label: Unlockable secrets that persist — not shipped
items.detail: Gates that survive refresh and can feed later pages. Today: local checklist/exercise only.

items.label: Durable reader choices — not shipped
items.detail: Branching that sticks and can be summarized for the author. Today: exercise is local-only and resets.

items.label: Thin data layer for entries — not shipped
items.detail: Store artifacts, publish status, and optional participation marks without growing a CMS. Today: git + JSON files.

items.label: Soft collaboration — not shipped
items.detail: Shared annotations, room reactions, co-author draft handoff. Today: git + PR for authors; nothing for readers.

blocks.heading: Parked until a draft proves the gap

columns.name: Reuse first
columns.detail: text, timeline, checklist, slideshow, exercise, series, tags, diagram, compact-table, and resource-list already cover arcs, personalities, hubs, and local participation.

columns.name: Build only when stuck
columns.detail: Add a widget or thin data piece when a real story-world draft cannot say the next true thing with the current bin—and when the addition stays renderer-thin.

blocks.title: Stay thin on purpose
blocks.body: Showmob remains linked pages and a shared renderer. Do not grow a novel CMS or MMO beside it. Sketch the world as data entries; let readers poke with local checks; only add widgets or persistence when a real draft proves the gap—and label shipped vs later, local vs durable, every time.

blocks.heading: Two-minute pitch: story world as data entries

slides.title: Entries, not a new app
slides.body: Characters, places, threads, items, and choices are ordinary Showmob pages. Readers get normal URLs.

slides.title: Four themes as the spine
slides.body: Character arcs, personalities, open-world hubs, and participatory data entries—sketched with the bin you have.

slides.title: Explore non-linearly
slides.body: Hubs, tags, and resource-lists for open browse; series when a path must stay ordered.

slides.title: Participate lightly, honestly
slides.body: Local exercise and checklist today—they reset. Durable marks wait for a thin data layer with evidence.

blocks.heading: Start with one entry and a hub
blocks.body: Publish one personality or place page, hang it from a hub with a resource-list, and put arc beats on a timeline. Use a checklist or exercise only if you want a local reader poke—and expect it to reset. Come back to this sketch when a real story-world draft forces a widget or data layer the current bin cannot cover.
